name: Resistor

claims.claim_text: Precision resistors specified at 0.1% tolerance with a low temperature coefficient, on the order of 25 ppm or less, are relied on to be in specification as delivered rather than screened on receipt, because verifying the tolerance and drift of each part would require stepping it through temperature.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's not like you get them and then you measure each one to make sure they're in spec
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: The Hard Work Hypothesis

claims.claim_text: At the top of the precision range the binding specification is temperature coefficient rather than initial tolerance: bulk-metal foil resistors reach 0.05 ppm per degree C, while 0.01% tolerance is unremarkable and 0.005% parts are obtainable for about twenty dollars.
claims.quote_verbatim: the TCR, the temperature coefficient
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Motors And Upgrading Sinclairs - Adapting Apraxiated Automobiles

claims.claim_text: A distributor shipping the wrong tolerance under a correct-looking part number is a live failure mode for precision analog work: a batch supplied as 0.1% parts was actually 1%, the parts were assembled onto boards and shipped, and the error surfaced as a roughly fifty percent test failure rate. A five percent failure rate might be written off; fifty percent is noticed.
claims.quote_verbatim: I got shipped a bad batch of resistors once. They were 1% tolerance instead of 0.1%
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Manufacturing By Wire And Skipping Testing - Calefacient Cuculine Cash

claims.claim_text: Reels of precision resistors are now shipped directly from the distributor to the assembler rather than double-handled through the designer, a change from the earlier practice of taking delivery first specifically to verify that the right part arrived.
claims.quote_verbatim: i get it sent straight to the manufacturer i don't double hand i used to double handle
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Our first in-person show

claims.claim_text: In a two-op-amp differential amplifier the resistor dividers on the two inputs must match, not merely be accurate: 1% resistors may leave gain error acceptable while badly degrading common-mode rejection ratio, because the rejection depends on the divider ratios being equal. High-voltage differential probes are built with trimmer resistors and trimmer capacitors adjusted at the factory for this reason.
claims.quote_verbatim: You might not have an issue with the gain, but you will have an issue with the common mode rejection ratio
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: New Year, New Gear

claims.claim_text: Resistor divider networks for precision instruments are negotiated against three coupled parameters, cost, initial tolerance and drift, so that loosening initial tolerance to 0.03% can buy a 10 ppm drift specification; the network vendor also modified the serpentine patterns of its thick-film elements to reduce stray capacitance. The overall accuracy specification of a digital multimeter is then the root-sum-square of the individual component contributions.
claims.quote_verbatim: the tradeoffs of cost versus tolerance versus drift
claims.speaker: Dave Taylor
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Dave Taylor - Multi-talented Meter Maker

claims.claim_text: Specifying resistors more tightly than the circuit requires is a design error with downstream cost: choosing E96 values or paying for 0.01% parts where the accuracy has no effect on the result degrades sourcing and raises cost for nothing, and one open-source design carried sixty different resistor values on its bill of materials. Judging where precision matters and where it does not is the discriminating skill.
claims.quote_verbatim: engineering's the art of knowing when something doesn't matter and when something matters
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Two and a Half Orders of Magnitude

claims.claim_text: Ten percent tolerance resistors are adequate for most designs; where a tighter part would help, adding another component is often the better trade than tightening the tolerance specification.
claims.quote_verbatim: we're always okay with using the 10% tolerance resistor
claims.speaker: Chris Taylor
claims.episode_title: An Interview with the SparkFun Team - Efficacious Engineering Ensemble

claims.claim_text: A resistor's intrinsic Johnson noise rises with its resistance value, which sets a floor on attenuator and signal-path design at low noise levels.
claims.quote_verbatim: the larger your resistance value, the higher your intrinsic noise
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Toasted Marshmallow Connectors

claims.claim_text: Resistors integrated on silicon are laser-trimmed during wafer and package test to raise the accuracy of the finished part, a step performed after wafer fabrication and before dicing, with the part tested again in package form.
claims.quote_verbatim: do a laser trim on the resistors to, you know, increase the accuracy
claims.speaker: Art Kay
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Art Kay

claims.claim_text: Wafers carry dedicated test sites, typically one at the centre and several on the periphery, populated with test transistors and resistors so the fab can confirm the process ran correctly; a more comprehensive post-fabrication measurement decides whether the wafers are used at all, and a whole wafer lot can be scrapped on that result.
claims.quote_verbatim: at the wafer fab, that's how they would make sure that the processing was being done correctly
claims.speaker: Art Kay
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Art Kay

claims.claim_text: On-chip trimming turns a twenty percent process spread into roughly one percent accuracy: the resistor is laid out as a chain of smaller chunks, a reference value is measured at production test, and links are fused to select the combination.
claims.quote_verbatim: you just chop that resistor up in the smaller chunks
claims.speaker: Jørgen Jakobsen
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jørgen Jakobsen

claims.claim_text: Self-trimming structures built into the silicon are the alternative to trimming at the wafer tester, and are chosen to avoid spending tester or boot-up time on the operation.
claims.quote_verbatim: automatic trimming so that you don't have to spend time on it on the, on the wafer tester
claims.speaker: Jørgen Jakobsen
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jørgen Jakobsen

claims.claim_text: Analog integrated circuit layout is drawn from three primitives, MOSFETs, resistors and capacitors, and the governing constraint is that absolute values do not repeat between wafers while neighbouring matched devices do. Process variation of a few microns in a layer's thickness can move device values by around ten percent on the next wafer, so circuits are designed as ratios of like components: a divider of three identically sized resistors gives the same output voltages regardless of their absolute value.
claims.quote_verbatim: you do the ratios between components, not precise values of components
claims.speaker: Matt Venn
claims.episode_title: Silicon Revolution with Matt Venn

claims.claim_text: Analog front-end modules increasingly place their dividers inside the package as laser-trimmed resistors, which are better than the discrete parts a designer would buy and remove the parasitics of separate packages, the pin inductance of each device, and the risk of two external resistors drifting in opposite directions and stacking their tolerances.
claims.quote_verbatim: laser trim resistors that are better than the ones you're going to want to buy and put outside
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Prior Art, Wafer Fabs and Guns - Whimsical Wafer Waffling

claims.claim_text: Resistors occupy a large area on a die, which is why TTL, whose logic depends on on-chip resistors, scaled poorly and was displaced by CMOS, where an inverter is two transistors and no resistance is required.
claims.quote_verbatim: things like resistors take up a physical large amount of die space
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ken Shirriff

claims.claim_text: Bill-of-materials optimisation trades component count against line-item count: two 10K resistors in parallel substitute for a more expensive 5K part and save a cent per unit, and a spare transistor wired as a diode avoids buying a reel of diodes. The deciding constraint is often feeder slots, since a design with thirty distinct parts requires an assembly machine that can hold thirty reels.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you put two 10Ks in parallel, you have a 5K resistor
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Loopback

claims.claim_text: Commodity passives are ordinarily specified on the bill of materials by package, tolerance and value rather than by manufacturer part number, because the assembler will supply standard stock and the brand is immaterial.
claims.quote_verbatim: You just put in 0.603, 1%, 1K
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Last Minute Decisions - Obdurate Onepercenter Obstacles

claims.claim_text: Contract manufacturers hold house parts for common passive values and run a matching step that maps a generic line such as a 1K 0805 to their own stock. The economics work against the customer specifying only generic values, since a board built entirely from house parts may leave the assembler no margin; naming a part number is the better practice.
claims.quote_verbatim: if it's all the same resistor as the house part, you know, we may not actually make any money on that board
claims.speaker: Chris Church
claims.episode_title: An interview with Macrofab - Macro Manufacturing Mechanization

claims.claim_text: Assembly houses stock common resistor values across the standard chip sizes, 0805, 0603 and 0402, so a small build need not buy full reels. The hazard is that a generic house part may not carry a specification the design depends on, such as a particular temperature coefficient or power rating.
claims.quote_verbatim: you've got to be careful that it's not a part which you need a specific, you know, spec for
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: EE Movies, Part Rants and SPICE.

claims.claim_text: Pick-and-place assembly consumes more parts than the board count implies, because components are lost when the reel is wound onto the machine, so excess must be supplied; ten or twenty spare parts is typical for cheap passives. Expensive components should be identified to the assembler so they are handled and loaded with care rather than wasted at the same rate.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can't give your manufacturer a reel of 100 resistors and expect them to populate 100 boards
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Solar Cells, SparkFun, TSMC - The Detroit Debunking

claims.claim_text: A design whose performance rests on a precision part should not be sent to an assembler who is free to substitute, because a four dollar resistor will be replaced with a four cent one and the substitution destroys the specification the product is sold on.
claims.quote_verbatim: they'll totally go out and source a $0.04 resistor
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Colin O'Flynn - Aspirated Adamantine Attacks

claims.claim_text: The cost structure of a precision instrument is dominated by a few parts and by verification: a single resistor at four dollars in volume can cost around twelve dollars at single-piece pricing, so low-volume builds absorb the difference directly out of margin, and the specification is backed by NIST-traceable calibration and purpose-built test gear that measures every unit. Copies of an open-source precision design built with lower-precision parts do not meet the original specification.
claims.quote_verbatim: one single resistor on there is four bucks
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: PLEASE be a die shrink

claims.claim_text: A single critical precision resistor can carry a two-month lead time at both the distributor and the manufacturer, which makes the reorder point for a product with such a part a supply-chain decision rather than a stock-level one.
claims.quote_verbatim: That critical resistor you need is two months lead time
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Risky Components and Hardware Innovation - Slipshod Shack Shutdown

claims.claim_text: Passive component shortages propagate across resistors, capacitors and low-complexity discretes together rather than affecting one part type, and have produced distributor reel prices doubling within a few months.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's just been general capacitor shortages and some resistor shortages
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Debugger vs Printeffer

claims.claim_text: Line-item count on a bill of materials is a recurring labour cost for anyone kitting a product by hand, and is a design parameter worth minimising up front; in practice the redesign to reduce it is rarely undertaken until a component goes obsolete and forces the design open again.
claims.quote_verbatim: the number one thing that I wish I had done a better job of when I did the initial design is just using a fewer line items in the bomb
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: MightyHohm For The Holidays - Kaiser Keyzer's Kits

claims.claim_text: The marginal cost of an additional passive on a board is negligible while the first one is not: getting a single resistor onto a board carries the design time, the board fabrication, the distributor order and the waiting, so the cost curve is dominated by fixed setup. Paying an assembly service several hundred dollars for the first few boards is usually worth it against that baseline.
claims.quote_verbatim: the first resistor on a board is a significant cost
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Use The Protection Circuit

claims.claim_text: A company component database multiplies variants of an apparently trivial part: a 10K resistor branches by schematic symbol style, then by tolerance grade at one percent, half a percent and 0.1 percent, then by temperature coefficient at 50, 15 or 10 ppm, and finally by the three IPC land-pattern density classes, so twenty entries for a 10K resistor accumulate and the wrong one gets picked. Raising a new part request, complete with specification, data sheet, an approved manufacturer part number and the required footprint variant, can consume half a working day.
claims.quote_verbatim: you'd end up with, you know, 20 10K resistors in the system
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Ludicrously High Frequency Interference

claims.claim_text: Tombstoning occurs when solder on one land pad reflows before the other and its surface tension lifts the chip component upright off the second pad. A production board was found under a stereo microscope with a resistor tombstoned so that one terminal made no contact at all, and the board still functioned.
claims.quote_verbatim: one pad of the resistor or one terminal of the resistor lifts up because the resistor kind of gets sucked upwards by the other pad
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Ardui...no Dave This Week?

claims.claim_text: Solder surface tension self-aligns small chip components during reflow, so a resistor placed approximately in position is drawn into place, and wafer-level chip-scale packages behave the same way. The hard case is a package with a large central ground pad, which is difficult to heat sufficiently and which will tilt the part if too much solder is applied there.
claims.quote_verbatim: If you get the resistor pretty much anywhere generally in the vicinity, it just kind of snaps into place
claims.speaker: Tim Ansell
claims.episode_title: Discussing the Open Source PDK with Tim Ansell

claims.claim_text: The workmanship standards allow far more placement error than intuition suggests: a chip resistor sitting roughly a third off its pads remains mechanically robust. The applicable standard depends on the product, and hobby assembly is judged by whether the circuit works rather than by aerospace-grade cleaning and inspection practice.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can have a resistor, like, I don't know, a third of the way off the pads and it's not going to come off ever
claims.speaker: Scott Driscoll
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Scott Driscoll - Impacable Interdisciplinary Inventor

claims.claim_text: Surface-mount parts are poorly suited to kits because each value must be cut from its carrier strip individually and then bagged and labelled, and chip capacitors carry no marking, so the builder must measure them. Through-hole parts carry printed values or colour codes, which makes them sortable, packageable and identifiable by the person assembling them.
claims.quote_verbatim: all the resistors have the color code on them
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: PCBs, Tektronix & Ham Radio - Habitual Handicraft Hangups

claims.claim_text: Through-hole components are held in their bandolier tape with glue, and leads pulled from the strip carry a residue that acts as an insulator; the leads must be trimmed before the part is inserted into a breadboard or the contact may not be made.
claims.quote_verbatim: you've got a layer of bloody glue on your pin. And it may not make contact
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Questioning Everyday Prototyping - Verrucose Vehicle Vitilitigation

claims.claim_text: Hand-placing the first boards of a design is the most direct design-for-manufacture feedback available, because the designer experiences the consequences of choices such as an unnecessarily small resistor package while placing them.
claims.quote_verbatim: the best way to do DFM is to experience the pain of your design decision
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Slapping Industries

claims.claim_text: Chip resistors picked off tape land at arbitrary angles, so hand assembly is done with every part deliberately rotated to a common orientation, which allows the values to be read in one pass during inspection instead of turning the board repeatedly. A larger package can be chosen deliberately, for example 1210 rather than an 0603, so that signals can be routed underneath the part.
claims.quote_verbatim: I will make sure it's rotated in the correct orientation. So they're all facing the same way so that I can go and just quickly scan the values
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Assembly Chat

claims.claim_text: Mislabelled or mixed component bags are caught during hand assembly by measuring the parts with a meter; a strip of 40.2K parts found in a bag marked 100K would otherwise have been fitted into a regulator feedback network, where the wrong divider value shows up as an output stuck well below its intended voltage.
claims.quote_verbatim: the 40k was in the feedback network of a different regulator
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Assembly Chat

claims.claim_text: A one-off value needed at a single position, such as the feedback reference resistor of a switching regulator, is hand-soldered after assembly rather than given a feeder on the placement machine.
claims.quote_verbatim: you wouldn't bother loading the pick and place if you just need that one resistor
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison
claims.episode_title: Meracious Mike Manuduction

claims.claim_text: Placement accuracy on a machine without vision is limited by the parts moving inside their tape pockets, so the part must be aligned after pickup. Two alignment methods exist, camera vision and laser measurement; a through-axis camera lets the operator see what the vacuum nozzle or laser is doing, and a laser line rotating the part measures its angular and X-Y offset from the nozzle centre so the machine can correct both at placement.
claims.quote_verbatim: There's tolerance. It doesn't fit in there tight. That resistor floats around
claims.speaker: Ryan O'Hara
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ryan O'Hara - Keyed, Kerfed Kapton

claims.claim_text: Locating design work next to manufacturing surfaces problems that do not appear on paper, such as a component position where the part consistently falls off the board during assembly, or an enclosure whose assembly time collapses from hours to minutes after one change.
claims.quote_verbatim: maybe that resistor doesn't belong there, because it always falls off the board
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: SpaceX, Enclosures & Startups - Urging Unemployment Ullagone

claims.claim_text: Where a design's resistors are within tolerance and its amplifiers are within their input bias specification, the remaining functional test adds little, so sample testing at one board in a hundred plus absorbing the cost of returns is a defensible production strategy for a low-value product.
claims.quote_verbatim: I can do just do sample testing. Like one in every hundred
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Manufacturing By Wire And Skipping Testing - Calefacient Cuculine Cash

claims.claim_text: Debugging by voltage stack-up follows current through known resistances: one amp through a ten ohm resistor must produce ten volts across it, and a smaller reading means the current is going somewhere else. The method holds for DC analog circuits and breaks down at high frequency, where capacitance shunts current away from the path being reasoned about.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's one amp of current flowing in this 10 ohm resistor and it's like okay you know there better be 10 volts at the top of that resistor
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Troubleshooting, PCBs and LEDs - Quaintized Quich Quelling

claims.claim_text: A quick health check on a working board is that series and pull-up resistors should show negligible voltage across them, since voltage across a resistor is dissipated power; bypass capacitors, by contrast, are expected to hold voltage. Where a drop is present, the resistance value converts it directly into a current figure.
claims.quote_verbatim: There should be no voltage across the resistor. If there's voltage across the resistor, you're wasting power
claims.episode_title: Measuring Current with Matt Liberty

claims.claim_text: Component swaps made during debugging should be recorded as they are made, with the hypothesis attached, because the alternative is a tray of desoldered resistors of unknown value and no record of which change produced which result.
claims.quote_verbatim: I wish I'd documented all those resistor changes I made to test this
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Rubber Ducking

claims.claim_text: Measuring a component in circuit can give a confidently wrong answer: a MOSFET read as 0.6 volts because of surrounding components and was taken for a bipolar transistor, and had to be removed and put on a component tester to identify. Once identified, the two 4.7 megohm resistors and the lower-value one below them made sense as a divider limiting the gate voltage to a level the MOSFET could survive.
claims.quote_verbatim: it tested out at 0.6 volts, you know, as if it was a bipolar transistor
claims.episode_title: The King of Trash with Big Clive

claims.claim_text: A resistor can be used as a controlled heat source rather than a circuit element: passing current through a resistor taped inside the flotation bag of a marine instrument burns a hole in the bag on command and scuttles the equipment.
claims.quote_verbatim: just put current through a resistor which was taped or in a little pocket on the inside of the inflatable floaty bag
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Let's Hear It For The Buoys - Vanishing Vessel Vexation

claims.claim_text: Burn-wire release mechanisms use the same principle in spacecraft: a meltable wire is wrapped around a resistor to hold a spring-loaded latch, and heating the resistor releases deployable solar panels and antenna elements on small satellites.
claims.quote_verbatim: you wrap a little bit of meltable wire around a resistor
claims.speaker: Dan Esparon
claims.episode_title: Satellite Design Engineering with Dan Esparon

claims.claim_text: Contact resistance in a switch is evaluated as a power dissipation problem: three volts across roughly an ohm is nine watts by V squared over R, dissipated inside a small mechanical switch, before the wiring resistance is counted.
claims.quote_verbatim: So three volts, you know, V squared on R, right?
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Voltnuts for Flashlights

claims.claim_text: A class of low-dropout regulator sets its output voltage with one resistor to ground instead of a feedback divider, by driving an internal constant current source of about ten microamps through it to develop the reference. Because that current is small, the internal source can be overridden by driving a voltage directly onto the set pin, which converts the part into a programmable supply.
claims.quote_verbatim: you set the output voltage with a single resistor. You don't need the traditional resistor divider on the output
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: BASIC, Chip companies & Robots - Pernicious Projects, Puppies in Peril

claims.claim_text: The same single-resistor scaling principle is extended in later regulators to auxiliary outputs: a current monitor and a die temperature output each have their range set by one external resistor, so the full-scale voltage can be matched to whatever analog-to-digital converter input range is available without external op amps or dividers.
claims.quote_verbatim: single resistor, you can scale the output voltage to anything you want because you just change the resistor value on the monitor pin
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Arduino, IndiGoGo and Hack-a-Day - Doodad Dealer Dancing

claims.claim_text: The minimum hardware change to replace a USB 2.0 port with a USB-C connector is to tie the two positions provided for the data pair together, wire them into the device as before, and add a pull-down resistor on the CC lines.
claims.quote_verbatim: just add a pull down resistor on the CC lines
claims.speaker: Jason Cerundolo
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jason Cerundolo

claims.claim_text: Electric vehicle charging on the Type 2 connector signals with two pins and no data protocol: one carries a one kilohertz square wave, and a resistor of a defined value inside the vehicle encodes the current level it can accept.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's basically a, a resistor in your car. And the value of that resistor load actually tells it
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Knob and Tube Wiring

claims.claim_text: A seven-segment display driven from logic outputs is properly designed with an individual dropper resistor per segment, so that the current through each segment is defined by calculation; the general rule is that any LED driven from a voltage source needs a series resistor.
claims.quote_verbatim: normally if you, if you're designing a seven segment display properly, you have individual lead dropper resistors on each segment
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Best way to find a leak

claims.claim_text: Board revision can be encoded in a set of resistors read by firmware at boot, which avoids separate builds or preprocessor branches per revision. The associated firmware discipline is to confine revision handling to a single board support or hardware abstraction file, so that a board change touches one file rather than every reference scattered through the code base.
claims.quote_verbatim: I'm reading a set of resistors at boot to determine what the revision is
claims.speaker: Phillip Johnston
claims.episode_title: Firmware for Hardware Engineers with Phillip Johnston

claims.claim_text: Resistors can be printed directly onto a board as conductive graphite by fabricators offering the process, with the required value specified as a design parameter rather than fitted as a component.
claims.quote_verbatim: you need a 10K resistor, we'll lay you down a 10K resistor
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An interview with Ariel Briner of Cartesian Co

claims.claim_text: Where an exact value is needed from a coarse preferred series, a search across the E24 range for pairs of resistors that combine to the target is done computationally, and the same tool shows how much the error falls if the design moves to the finer E96 series.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can combine these two resistors from the E24 range to give you this particular tolerance
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Art Kay

claims.claim_text: Current sensing with a small series resistor, on the order of 0.1 ohm, is the standard method borrowed from voltage regulator short-circuit protection, and adding half an ohm in series with a coil that already has ohms of resistance is an acceptable perturbation.
claims.quote_verbatim: You put it like a 0.1 ohm and it doesn't really harm the regulator too much because it's negligible voltage drop
claims.speaker: Ron Quan
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ron Quan - Tenacious Transistor Teacher

claims.claim_text: Measuring current by putting a resistor in line and reading it with an oscilloscope is limited by what the measurement is referenced to: touching the probe ground to one side ties the measurement to the instrument's earth ground and introduces errors, so a genuine differential probe is required for a correct reading.
claims.quote_verbatim: The problem is how, what are you measuring across?
claims.episode_title: The Joulescope Upgrade with Matt Liberty

claims.claim_text: SPICE unit suffixes are a standing trap: M denotes milli and Meg denotes mega, so a resistor entered as one M is a thousand times smaller than intended and the simulation result is wrong rather than obviously broken.
claims.quote_verbatim: You've got to put Meg, yeah
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Fremescent Floccose Fortification

claims.claim_text: Power rating governs stock as much as value does: a bench holding every E96 value in quarter-watt parts still cannot build a ten ohm load capable of dissipating the power of a battery discharge test, because that requires one-watt parts or on the order of a hundred quarter-watt resistors in parallel.
claims.quote_verbatim: so i can't use a quarter watt resistor right so i've got big stocks of quarter watt
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Sowing Discord

claims.claim_text: Over-the-counter component supply persists in a small number of distributors, where a staffed counter in the basement takes a spoken specification such as a quarter-watt one kilohm resistor and fetches the part, but the model is disappearing.
claims.quote_verbatim: you want a resistor, you go there like, okay, I need that resistor, uh, quarter Watts, one kilo ohm and they get it for you
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Great Scott

claims.claim_text: Multimeters that warn when the probe is in the wrong jack detect it with a split current jack and a high-value resistor of around five megohms feeding a high-impedance threshold detector. Because the sensing node is high impedance, dirt, grime or moisture inside the jack produces the warning with nothing plugged in; cleaning the jacks with alcohol restores correct behaviour.
claims.quote_verbatim: a five mega resistor goes on real, you know, high impedance value resistor goes off to then a high impedance
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: The Tandy Train

claims.claim_text: A minimal USB human interface device implant reduces to three resistors, two zener diodes and an ATtiny microcontroller, arrived at by cannibalising existing development boards to find the smallest circuit that retains the function, which frees the remaining volume for other hardware.
claims.quote_verbatim: Got it down to, what, three resistors, two zener diodes, the ATtiny itself
claims.speaker: Mike Grover
claims.episode_title: An Interview with MG (Mike Grover)

claims.claim_text: Dedicated LED driver chips are difficult to design out precisely because the alternative, driving each LED from a microcontroller pin, requires an external series resistor per LED and cannot reproduce the driver's current control.
claims.quote_verbatim: you'd have to have an external resistor for each LED
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Thousands Of Dependencies

claims.claim_text: Indicator LED brightness is normally set empirically rather than engineered: a nominal series resistor such as 1K is fitted, the assembled product is judged by eye, and the value is changed on the bill of materials afterwards if it is wrong, which is why photometric characterisation at design time solves a problem most designers do not have.
claims.quote_verbatim: most designers are content just to change the resistor value after the fact
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: All Heat, No Useful Work

claims.claim_text: A load resistor absorbing the output of a high-current power module glows visibly, and colour is used as the working temperature indicator during test, with orange acceptable and white the point at which the test is stopped.
claims.quote_verbatim: you put it into a resistor and that resistor usually starts glowing
claims.speaker: Fredrik Kensander
claims.episode_title: High Current Power Supplies with Fredrik Kensander

claims.claim_text: Cost-optimised consumer products are poor material for learning circuit theory but good material for learning manufacturing improvisation, since they contain expedients such as a resistor soldered on edge purely as a mechanical brace for a potentiometer. A more expensive product is more likely to contain a recognisable application-note circuit and therefore more transferable theory.
claims.quote_verbatim: they didn't decide to actually use it as a resistor. They just soldered it on edge to provide like a physical balance
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Eating An Elephant

claims.claim_text: Extreme unit-cost constraints change the design process qualitatively rather than quantitatively: in toy design a resistor costing a hundredth of a cent cannot simply be added, and cost reduction is the rewarded outcome, in contrast to industries where time to market dominates.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can't put in an extra resistor because it's going to cost 0.01 cents
claims.speaker: Jeri Ellsworth
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jeri Ellsworth - The Ternary Tussle

claims.claim_text: Electronic rules of thumb originate in the era before cheap calculation, when working out a resistor value with a slide rule was expensive enough that engineers instead picked a value from the bench, observed the behaviour and adjusted in the direction indicated.
claims.quote_verbatim: doing electronics calculations without a calculator is quite hard
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Apple HQ and Vintage Arcade Games - The Mothership Manifesto

claims.claim_text: Breadboards that insert protective series resistance keep beginners from destroying LEDs, but conceal the need for a current-limiting resistor, so parts fail as soon as the circuit is transferred to a real board.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's just enough resistance to keep them from frying
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: A Jumperless Breadboard with Kevin Cappuccio

claims.claim_text: A resistor, an LED and a battery are sufficient material for a genuine sense of discovery in electronics, and a design practice can be built on presenting circuits that way rather than on a single-board computer running an operating system.
claims.quote_verbatim: you could do that with LED and a battery and a resistor. You can learn a lot from that
claims.speaker: Saar Drimer
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Saar Drimer
